Subject: Monthly KPI variance & rollup — latency/cost/uptime highlights (Nov)

Team,

Attaching the Nov KPI rollup and the raw exports. High-level callouts before the handoffs:

- Latency: P95 generation increased ~12% vs. Oct (from 210ms to ~235ms). The distribution shows tail increases concentrated during 18:00-22:00 UTC window (see "latency_by_hour" sheet).
- Cost: Platform token spend up 16% month-over-month; unit-cost per active session is +9% driven by longer context/session lengths and fewer cache hits for long conversations.
- Uptime: 99.96% for the month — one 35-minute blip on 2026-11-19 tied to a routing misconfiguration; SLA impact minimal but we need to close runbook gaps.
- Usage: MAU +18%, embeddings requests spiked due to 2 large partner jobs (Acme) mid-month.

Asks:
1) Markus — please own the latency deep-dive (kernel selection and batching metrics). Can you confirm whether the 18:00-22:00 UTC window maps to a specific customer? If not, prioritize kernel trace capture for next peak.
2) Rishi — cost mitigation options: I want a short list (3 items) by EOD Thu with estimated 30/60/90 day impact. Consider model quantization A/B and cache TTL adjustments.
3) Laura — can you draft a rollback-safe canary plan for lightweight quantization (int8) to validate output fidelity vs cost for 5% of traffic? Put the draft in the QBR slide deck.
4) Evelyn — own a postmortem for the 11/19 routing blip; include timeline, root cause, and runbook edits.

Attachments: redwood_kpi_dash_nov2026.pdf, kpi_raw_nov2026.csv, incidents_2026-11.log

I want these items summarized in the QBR deck by Friday so we can surface to execs next week. If anyone needs to reassign, call it out here.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel

Thanks, Monica — quick notes after a first pass on the export:

- Early signal looks like a combination of larger prompts (token count per request up ~14%) and a drop in prefix-cache hit rates for a subset of models. The kernel selection logs show a few fallbacks to generic kernels during peak bursts.
- I'll instrument an additional trace (microsecond granularity) for the 12/02 and 12/03 peaks. If we can reproduce, we should be able to confirm whether the kernel fallback is the dominant factor.
- On the Acme spike: ops@cloudvendor.com confirms two batch jobs that pushed embeddings concurrently for 6 hours on 11/14; that caused node saturation in us-west and amplified tail latency. I've looped in CloudOps below for capacity follow-up.

Action: I'll deliver an initial hypothesis + prioritized checklist by EOD Wed.

-Markus

Couple of practical items from infra/rollout POV:

- Canary plan outline (high level):
  * Target: 5% production traffic on an isolated pool for 72 hours.
  * Metrics to gate: P95/P99 gen latency, output-quality regression (BLEU/embedding similarity spot checks), error rate, cost per 1k tokens.
  * Fallback: automatic rollback to current model routing after 3 consecutive gating failures or >2x error rate.
  * Safety net: pin affected customer traffic (Acme) to a fallback region for the pilot window to avoid cross-impact.

- For the 11/19 blip postmortem, Evelyn: include the ASG scaling logs and the routing table snapshot. That will help us avoid ambiguity about whether it was a routing decision or ASG scaling lag.

- I created a stub slide in the shared deck for the canary plan: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/KPI/Nov2026/canary-plan-draft

I'll add estimated rollout time (2-3 weeks including validation) and an A/B test plan for quality checks.

— Laura
